syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish elastic from plastic behaviour of bodies under deforming forces.
Define stress and the longitudinal, shearing and volume strains and compute simple strains.

topics.title: Hooke's law and the stress-strain curve

concepts.learning_objective: State Hooke's law and the region of the stress-strain curve in which it holds.
Interpret the elastic limit, yield point, permanent set and fracture on a stress-strain curve.
Classify materials as ductile, brittle or elastomers from their stress-strain behaviour.
Define Young's modulus and identify the states of matter for which it is meaningful.
Use F/A = Y(Delta L/L) to calculate and compare extensions of wires.
Define the shear modulus and use it to find the displacement under a tangential force.
Define the bulk modulus and calculate the fractional change in volume under hydraulic pressure.

topics.title: Poisson's ratio and elastic potential energy

concepts.learning_objective: Define Poisson's ratio and calculate it from lateral and longitudinal strains.
Calculate the elastic potential energy stored in a stretched wire.

topics.title: Applications of elastic behaviour of materials

concepts.learning_objective: Estimate the minimum cross-section of a crane rope from the yield strength.
Use the sag relation for a centrally loaded beam to explain beam design.
Estimate the maximum height of a mountain from the elastic limit of rock.

topics.title: Pressure, Pascal's law and hydraulic machines

concepts.learning_objective: Define pressure and state Pascal's law for an enclosed fluid at rest.
Apply Pascal's law to find the force multiplication in a hydraulic lift or brake.

topics.title: Variation of pressure with depth, atmospheric and gauge pressure

concepts.learning_objective: Use P = Pa + rho g h to find absolute and gauge pressure at a depth in a liquid.
Explain how a barometer or manometer measures atmospheric and gauge pressure.

topics.title: Streamline flow and the equation of continuity

concepts.learning_objective: Describe steady (streamline) flow and the properties of streamlines.
Apply Av = constant to relate flow speed and cross-sectional area.
State Bernoulli's principle and relate it to conservation of energy and dynamic lift.
Use Torricelli's law and Bernoulli's equation to calculate speed of efflux and lift.
Define the coefficient of viscosity and describe how it varies with temperature.
Use Stokes' law to find the viscous drag and terminal velocity of a sphere.

topics.title: Surface tension, surface energy and angle of contact

concepts.learning_objective: Relate surface tension to surface energy and calculate work done in stretching a film.
Explain wetting and non-wetting using the angle of contact.
Calculate the excess pressure inside a liquid drop and a soap bubble.
Use h = 2S cos(theta)/(rho g a) to explain and calculate capillary rise.

topics.title: Temperature, heat and measurement of temperature

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish temperature as a measure of hotness from heat as energy transferred due to a temperature difference.
Convert temperatures between the Celsius, Fahrenheit and arbitrary linear scales using fixed points.
Apply the ideal-gas equation PV = muRT to a sample of low-density gas.
Explain how a constant-volume gas thermometer leads to absolute zero and the Kelvin scale.
Use the coefficients of linear and volume expansion and the relation between them.
Describe the anomalous expansion of water and its consequence for aquatic life.
Calculate the thermal stress in a rod whose expansion is prevented.
Define specific heat capacity and use Q = ms(delta T).
Apply the principle that heat lost equals heat gained in an isolated system.

topics.title: Change of state and latent heat

concepts.learning_objective: Describe melting, boiling, sublimation and the effect of pressure on the boiling point.
Use Q = mL for latent heats of fusion and vaporisation.
Use H = KA(TC - TD)/L for steady-state conduction through a rod.
Explain natural and forced convection with everyday examples such as sea breeze.

topics.title: Radiation, blackbody radiation and Newton's law of cooling

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Wien's displacement law and the Stefan-Boltzmann law.
Apply Newton's law of cooling to estimate cooling times for small temperature differences.

topics.title: Thermal equilibrium and the Zeroth Law

concepts.learning_objective: Explain thermal equilibrium as the state in which macroscopic variables of systems in thermal contact stop changing.
State the Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics and explain how it leads to the concept of temperature.
Describe internal energy as the sum of molecular kinetic and potential energies and as a state variable.
Distinguish heat and work as modes of energy transfer that are not state variables.
State the First Law as dQ = dU + dW and apply its sign conventions.
Apply the First Law to calculate changes in internal energy, heat or work.
Define specific and molar heat capacity and use them to compute heat exchanged.
Use the relation Cp - Cv = R for an ideal gas and the 3R value for solids.

topics.title: Thermodynamic state variables and equation of state

concepts.learning_objective: Identify state variables and recognise that they describe only equilibrium states.
Classify thermodynamic variables as extensive or intensive.
Describe quasi-static and isothermal processes and compute work in an isothermal change.
Apply PV^gamma = constant to adiabatic processes of an ideal gas.
Apply the First Law to isochoric, isobaric and cyclic processes.

topics.title: Second Law; reversible and irreversible processes

concepts.learning_objective: State the Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements of the Second Law.
Explain the conditions for reversibility and the causes of irreversibility.
Describe the four steps of the Carnot cycle and why they are chosen.
Calculate the efficiency of a Carnot engine using 1 - T2/T1.
Relate Dalton's atomic theory, Gay Lussac's law and Avogadro's law to the molecular picture of matter.
Compare atomic size, interatomic spacing and mean free path in solids, liquids and gases.
Use the ideal gas equation in its forms PV = muRT, P = n kB T and P = rho RT/M0.
Apply Boyle's law, Charles' law and Dalton's law of partial pressures to gas samples.
Explain when real gases approach ideal gas behaviour and interpret PV/T versus P plots.

topics.title: Kinetic theory of an ideal gas: pressure

concepts.learning_objective: State the assumptions of the kinetic model of an ideal gas.
Derive and apply P = (1/3) n m <v^2> and PV = (2/3) E.
Relate the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule to absolute temperature.
Calculate and compare root mean square speeds of gas molecules.
Count translational, rotational and vibrational degrees of freedom of molecules.
Apply the law of equipartition to find the average energy of molecules and gas samples.
Predict Cv, Cp and gamma for monatomic, diatomic and polyatomic gases using equipartition.
Explain why the molar specific heat of most solids is close to 3R.
State and apply the expression for mean free path l = 1/(sqrt2 n pi d^2).
Relate mean free path, average speed and collision frequency, and explain slow diffusion of gases.

topics.title: Periodic and oscillatory motions: period, frequency and displacement

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish periodic motion from oscillatory motion with everyday examples.
Relate period and frequency and use the hertz as the unit of frequency.

topics.title: Simple harmonic motion: amplitude, phase and angular frequency

concepts.learning_objective: Identify amplitude, phase and phase constant in x(t) = A cos(omega t + phi).
Use omega = 2 pi / T to relate angular frequency and period.

topics.title: Simple harmonic motion and uniform circular motion

concepts.learning_objective: Explain SHM as the projection of uniform circular motion on a diameter.

topics.title: Velocity, acceleration and the force law in SHM

concepts.learning_objective: Obtain v = -omega A sin(omega t + phi) and a = -omega^2 x and their maximum values.
Apply F = -kx and omega = sqrt(k/m) to a linear oscillator such as a spring-mass system.
Express K and U of an oscillator as functions of displacement and time.
Use the constancy of E = (1/2)kA^2 to find speeds and energy shares.
Use T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) and its independence from mass and amplitude.
Explain why a pendulum is simple harmonic only for small angular displacements.

topics.title: Mechanical waves; transverse and longitudinal waves

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a mechanical wave transfers a disturbance and energy through an elastic medium without bulk flow of matter.
Distinguish transverse and longitudinal waves and identify the media that can support each.

topics.title: Displacement relation in a progressive wave

concepts.learning_objective: Identify amplitude, phase, angular wave number and angular frequency in y = a sin(kx - wt + phi).
Relate wavelength to k and period and frequency to w, and find phase differences between points.

topics.title: Speed of a travelling wave and waves on a string

concepts.learning_objective: Apply v = w/k = lambda nu and recognise that the medium fixes speed while the source fixes frequency.
Calculate the speed of a transverse wave on a string from its tension and linear mass density.
Use v = sqrt(B/rho) and v = sqrt(Y/rho) to explain the speed of longitudinal waves in fluids and solids.
Explain Newton's formula for the speed of sound in a gas and the Laplace correction.
State the principle of superposition for overlapping waves and pulses.
Find the resultant amplitude 2a cos(phi/2) of two identical waves differing in phase.

topics.title: Reflection of waves, standing waves and normal modes

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the phase change on reflection at rigid and open boundaries.
Locate nodes and antinodes and find the normal modes of a string fixed at both ends.
Find the normal modes of air columns closed at one end and open at both ends.
Explain the formation of beats and calculate beat frequency and unknown frequencies from beat data.
